accounting_note: Research is a benchmark at published statistical extents. Opening is an independent authority with retained legacy accounts. Differences involving unmatched extents, dates or sources are arithmetic and cannot locate people.

research_units.name: Algeria
research_units.note: Appendix I uses Maravall-Buckwalter's corrected population, anchored on the 1906 return including the Territories of the South. Their opening-day extent remains unresolved. Metropolitan France excludes Algeria.

research_units.name: Angola
research_units.note: The political candidates require a review of source coverage and territorial exclusions.

research_units.name: Basutoland
research_units.note: Both refer to Basutoland outside the four South African polities. The opening interpolates the 1891 and 1904 returns after the 1901 census was suspended.

research_units.name: Bechuanaland

research_units.name: Belgium Congo

research_units.name: British East Africa

research_units.name: Cape Verde (Portuguese Africa)

research_units.name: Liberia

research_units.name: Madagascar

research_units.name: Mauritius

research_units.name: Morocco
research_units.note: Appendix I projects backwards from separate French and northern Spanish protectorate counts plus Tangier. Adequacy of the southern frontier coverage for the 1900 Sultanate remains unresolved. Spanish Sahara, Ceuta and Melilla have separate study series.

research_units.name: Mozambique (Portuguese Africa)

research_units.name: Réunion

research_units.name: Rwanda and Burundi

research_units.name: Tunisia

research_units.name: Dutch East Indies (Indonesia)
research_units.note: Java, the Outer Islands and western New Guinea. Excludes East Timor, the British Borneo territories and Brunei. Separate from the Netherlands. The research account balance remains an arithmetic unlocated pool including any date, coverage or definition differences. It does not establish the total of the Outer Islands.

research_units.name: Formosa (Taiwan)
research_units.note: Taiwan and Penghu under Japanese administration. Separate from the Japanese home islands and the Qing control.

research_units.note: Both cover Belgium on its 1900 boundary, separate from the Netherlands, the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and Congo Free State. The nine-province census series counts usual residents. The research series aims at present population.

research_units.name: Finland
research_units.note: Empire excluding Finland. 1897 census extrapolated by Sifman's correction for duplicated movers; Khiva and Bukhara have a separate source series. / Grand Duchy of Finland under Russian crown. Separate study unit and excluded from Russian census total.

research_units.name: France
research_units.note: Metropolitan departments on the 1900 boundary. Alsace–Lorraine belongs to the German return. Colonies are outside both metropolitan controls.

research_units.name: Norway
research_units.note: Sweden and Norway, separately tabulated within their political union.

research_units.name: Ottoman (Balkans)
research_units.note: Ottoman European provinces.

research_units.name: Portugal
research_units.note: Mainland Portugal, the Azores and Madeira, with overseas possessions excluded. The opening interpolates the 1890 and 1900 official census returns of persons present.

research_units.name: Romania
research_units.note: The Romanian Old Kingdom, before the territorial gains of 1913 and 1918. Its adopted count is the 1899 census of legal residents.

research_units.name: Russia Empire/USSR
research_units.note: Empire excluding Finland. 1897 census extrapolated by Sifman's correction for duplicated movers; Khiva and Bukhara have a separate source series. / Grand Duchy of Finland under Russian crown. Separate study unit and excluded from Russian census total.

research_units.name: Serbia/Yugoslavia
research_units.note: 1900 Kingdom of Serbia. Historical Statistics Serbia from 1879 to 1910; Montenegro remains separate.

research_units.name: Spain
research_units.note: Spain including Canary and Balearic Islands (Appendix I note 129). Overseas possessions excluded.

research_units.name: Sweden
research_units.note: Sweden and Norway, separately tabulated within their political union.

research_units.name: Switzerland
research_units.note: The historical cantons and half cantons; the opening uses the federal resident-population comparison of 1888 and 1900.

research_units.name: United Kingdom
research_units.note: Great Britain and all Ireland. Crown Dependencies and overseas possessions are outside both controls.

research_units.name: Australia
research_units.note: Six pre-federation colonies combined under WWO economic alias. Study explicitly adds the Smith Aboriginal reconstruction; state-level ABS figures have narrower enumeration. The ABS-counted population is separated by colony. The arithmetic balance between the two historical series remains geographically unallocated. It cannot identify the size or distribution of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander populations.

research_units.name: Hawai
research_units.note: The Hawaiian Islands remain a separate Oceania series. The opening uses actual census reference dates.

research_units.name: New Zeland
research_units.note: The opening includes the contemporary official carry-forward of Māori population. Its non-Māori district estimates do not cover the whole group. Both figures are estimates.

research_units.name: Melanesia
research_units.note: The independent colony return covers Fiji and Rotuma. Federico–Tena also includes New Caledonia, New Hebrides, eastern New Guinea and Solomon Islands in Melanesia. Subtracting the opening figure cannot identify any of those populations.

research_units.name: Micronesia
research_units.note: The regional total includes Guam and other archipelagos. A mutually exclusive island allocation is unavailable.

research_units.name: Polynesia
research_units.note: Archipelago-level allocation and islands outside the map catalogue require separate controls.

research_units.name: United Arab Emirates
research_units.note: V4 Trucial coast series. V5 summary includes an equivalent residual but V5 country column is absent.

The Regency of Tunis under the French protectorate. Separate from metropolitan France, Algeria and the retained Ottoman economy. Appendix I uses a modeled growth rate before 1906 because early enumerations covered the French population only. Adopt the territorial reconstruction without assigning provincial populations.
Perez-Brignoli uses the Chilean 1895 and 1907 benchmarks; the interpolated country figure is a reconstruction.
Bahamas colony. Turks and Caicos form a separate research series. Bulmer-Thomas Tables A.1 and C.1.
Maltese islands series from Statistical Yearbook Malta; separate from United Kingdom.

Cape Verde archipelago, separate from Portuguese Guinea, São Tomé and metropolitan Portugal. Appendix I p. 47 uses Carreira p. 42 and adjusts interpolations for famines. The 1895 and 1900 government island series and retrospective INE total provide separate comparators.

Jamaica island. Cayman and Turks and Caicos are separate study series. Appendix I uses Bulmer-Thomas Tables A.1 and C.1. Jamaica did not take the 1901 imperial census, so the opening uses the historical reconstruction.
The two islands were administered together at opening. Bulmer-Thomas tabulates both separately before 1900 and jointly thereafter.
Barbados island, independent of the Windward Islands statistical series. Bulmer-Thomas Tables A.1 and C.1.

Madagascar and near-shore dependencies in the 1900 colony. Nosy Be and Sainte-Marie are included and the latter is missing from the simplified map outline. Comoros, Mayotte and Reunion are separate research units. The reconstructed total uses the Frankema–Jerven series. The near-date administrative alternatives omit some regions or categories.
Puerto Rico separately enumerated under US administration; independent 1899 War Department census. Continental US opening excludes it.
Martinique island. Separate from the metropolitan France opening and from Guadeloupe. Bulmer-Thomas series includes 1894 and 1900, before the 1902 eruption.

British Honduras within colonial boundaries, separate from Honduras, Guatemala and Mexico. Appendix I uses Bulmer-Thomas Tables A.1 and C.1 and compares with Kuczynski vol. III p. 4 and the 1901 colonial census.

Java, the Outer Islands and western New Guinea. Excludes East Timor, the British Borneo territories and Brunei. Separate from the Netherlands. Country study pp. 3–4 and workbook rows 101–102 (https://doi.org/10.21950/E09BKS); Appendix I pp. 73–75. Java and Madura are a distinct civilian statistical subdivision. The research account balance remains an arithmetic unlocated pool including any date, coverage or definition differences. It does not establish the total of the Outer Islands.
Home islands. Table 2.1 of Historical Statistics of Japan and the 1920 census anchor. Taiwan is a separate study series and WWO dependency.
Iceland, enumerated separately from the Danish metropole. Danish yearbook provides independent 1901 territorial control.
Kingdom after annexation of Rome and Veneto, before acquisition of Austrian territories. Colonies separate.
Grand Duchy after the 1839 partition. Use the established WWO economic alias for the same political unit.
1900 Kingdom of Serbia. Historical Statistics Serbia from 1879 to 1910; Montenegro remains separate.
Spain including Canary and Balearic Islands (Appendix I note 129). Overseas possessions excluded.

Korean peninsula before annexation, separate from the Japanese home islands and Taiwan. Kwon and Shin reconstruct the population using revised 1910 benchmarks and earlier population registers. Under-registration is material.
Bulgaria with Eastern Rumelia after 1885; historical statistics and census, before the Balkan Wars.

Empire excluding Finland. 1897 census extrapolated by Sifman's correction for duplicated movers; Khiva and Bukhara have a separate source series. / Grand Duchy of Finland under Russian crown. Separate study unit and excluded from Russian census total.
Sweden and Norway, separately tabulated within their political union.
Taiwan and Penghu under Japanese administration. Separate from the Japanese home islands and the Qing control.

The independent republic, separate from Argentina and Brazil. Appendix I uses the national estimate from Bulmer-Thomas Table 3.1. Uruguay's statistical office records no general census between 1860 and 1908.
